ideas.description: Exploit: stack the free lever (the freeze) with the cheapest accuracy booster (epochs). Start from the E027 tip and apply E028's freeze exactly as committed in fcacfc6. Group-1 conv filters, the whitening bias and group-1 BN params get their own param groups. Their LR follows the global triangle to its peak, then decays linearly to 0 at 75% of total steps. For the last 25% of steps, use the truncated compiled 32 px step: group-1 output detached, and no group-1 or whitening backward or update. Group-1 BN stays in train mode and Lookahead averages every param. Then change only the step count: 8.75 to 9.25 true epochs (about 231 steps at batch 2000). Read the exact count from the code. The resolution phases (20/24/28/32 at 15/25/30/30%), the freeze point (75%), and the LR and Lookahead schedules stay fixed fractions of the new total. Capture full and truncated 32 px variants in build with channels_last synthetic tensors, with error_on_recompile on. In the same session, run held-out seeds 3–12. Keep if seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 and held-out ≥ 0.7545. Do not re-roll RNG streams to chase seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time about 5.65–5.75 s (E028's 5.36 s plus about 0.3–0.35 s for 0.5 epoch, part of it in cheap frozen steps), which beats E027 (5.88 s) by 2–4%. Held-out mean about 0.7540–0.7555 (E028's 0.7525 plus 0.5 epoch × 0.37–0.44 pp/epoch). Seeds 0–2 clear 0.753 with about 60–75% probability. If held-out is below 0.7535, the freeze has a hidden cost at the longer schedule; then try 9.5 epochs only if it still projects under 5.85 s.

ideas.description: Exploit and crux test (W5: does a math-identical change keep the tip's per-seed outcomes?). Base: the current tip (E027, or the H2.6.2 successor if kept). Change only systems work in prepare, keeping every number bit-identical. (1) Move the training images to the GPU as uint8 and do the float conversion, normalization and channels_last/fp16 cast on the GPU, in the same op order and dtype the CPU path uses now. (2) In build, run prepare's GPU kernels once on synthetic uint8 tensors of the real shape: the whitening patch extraction and eigendecomposition, the normalization and the allocations. This removes trial 0's 0.21 s first-call cost. The whitening is still computed from the same images as now; do not subsample. Before launching, check offline with torch.equal that the normalized train tensor and the whitening weights equal the current ones. If they don't, adjust the op order until they do, or abandon. Record per-trial prepare time.
ideas.expected: Per-seed accuracies bit-identical to the base (to be verified, which settles W5's crux). Mean time falls 0.03–0.10 s (prepare mean about 0.11 to about 0.04–0.06 s, mostly trial 0), i.e. 0.5–1.5%. If the tensors can't be made bit-identical, report that and fall back to a held-out-judged version.

ideas.description: Exploit. First read the code. If the whitening bias already stops training before 25% of steps, close H2.6.3 without a run. Otherwise, on the H2.6.2 successor (or E027 if it is not kept), stop the whitening bias's gradient after 20% of steps (Hiverge; airbench96 trains it for 3/45 epochs). Use a third compiled step variant in which the whitening output is detached, so no input-grad of group 1's first conv and no whitening backward on the 31×31 maps. Group 1 still trains normally until the freeze. Anneal the whitening-bias LR to 0 by 20% of steps. Capture the new variant at every resolution it runs at (20/24/28/32 px) in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time falls 1–3% (about 0.06–0.15 s). It removes only the stem's input-grad and the bias-grad reduction on the largest maps between 20% and 75% of steps. Held-out mean within ±0.1 pp of the base. A loss above 0.15 pp means the bias keeps adapting to resolution switches; the 20/24/28 px phases happen after 20%.

ideas.description: Exploit, the freeze dose. Run only once the H2.6.2 successor is kept, and on it. Move the group-1 and whitening-bias freeze start from 75% to 60% of steps. The group-1 LR is annealed to 0 by 60%. Everything else is unchanged, including the step count, resolution phases and LR/Lookahead schedules. The truncated step now also runs during the last 10% of the 28 px phase (60–70%), so capture a truncated 28 px variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. Keep if held-out ≥ 0.7545 and seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753, or if the held-out loss is ≤ 0.1 pp and a follow-up epoch top-up is planned.
ideas.expected: Time falls 3–5% (about 0.17–0.25 s, about 33 more truncated steps at about 7–9.5 ms each), to about 5.45–5.55 s. Held-out mean falls 0–0.2 pp. A loss of 0.15 pp or less beats the epoch dial (about 1.5–2.7 s/pp) and supports H2.6.4. A loss above 0.25 pp means group 1 still learns usefully at 60–75% of a 9-epoch CIFAR-100 run, and the freeze stays at 75%.

ideas.description: Validation diagnostic, with no recipe change. Run it immediately after a candidate tip is kept (the H2.6.2 successor, or whatever is the tip once H2.6.3/H3.2.1 are stacked). Seeds 3–12 have driven about 10 keep decisions and carry a winner's curse. Run the committed recipe offline on fresh seeds 13–22 through the harness (benchmark.run --seed 13 --n 10). Record per-seed accuracy, mean and std, and the pooled 20-seed mean with its SE. Do not edit submissions/arena/.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged. The fresh mean is within 0.15 pp of the seeds 3–12 mean (expected offset about −0.05 pp from selection). Pooled 20-seed mean ≥ 0.753 supports H4.3.2, and the candidate has about 0.3 pp of headroom over the 40-seed bar of 0.75. If the fresh mean is below 0.752, further time cuts must stop until accuracy is bought back.

ideas.description: Explore, the next memory-bound lever on the frozen stem. On the H2.6.2 successor (or the freeze recipe in fcacfc6), at the freeze point: run one no-grad train-mode forward of group 1 over the current batch to set its BN running stats. Use the existing buffers if their values are already the frozen-phase stats. Then, for the frozen phase, put group-1 BN in eval mode and fold scale and shift into the conv weights and biases (done inside timed train, once). The truncated step then runs group 1 as conv+bias+GELU under no_grad, with no BN statistics reductions on the 31×31 maps. Lookahead still averages the unfolded params. Keep the unfolded copies so the final weights and BN buffers stay consistent: either fold only in the compiled frozen forward, or unfold before the final copy. Eval uses the standard model. Capture the new truncated variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time falls 1.5–3% (about 0.08–0.15 s) beyond the base. The 3 BN reductions and normalizations on 128×31×31 maps go away from about 55 frozen steps. Held-out within ±0.15 pp: eval-mode BN removes batch-stat noise in the frozen layers, which may even help slightly. A saving under 1% refutes H2.6.5 and says the frozen forward is conv-bound, not BN-bound.

ideas.description: Explore diagnostic, with no recipe change. It sets the value of the remaining stem levers (H2.6.4/H2.6.5/H2.6.3) and the PCIe-transfer caveat in H4.3. Offline, run torch.profiler on the tip's compiled 32 px full step and truncated step, and on the 24 px step, with batch 2000 and synthetic channels_last data. Record GPU time by kernel class (conv GEMM fwd/dgrad/wgrad, BN, GELU, pool, elementwise, Muon NS, Lookahead) and by layer group (whitening, group 1, 2, 3, head). Also record achieved conv TFLOP/s per group. Write the table to the notebook and label each kept lever as compute-bound or bandwidth-bound. Do not edit submissions/arena/.
ideas.expected: No change to time or accuracy. Predicted: non-GEMM kernels take ≥30% of the 32 px full step. Whitening plus group 1 take ≥35% of it, against about 20% of MACs. Group-3 convs run below 70 TFLOP/s. If non-GEMM is under 20%, H6.3 is refuted and H2.6.5 drops to priority 1.

ideas.description: Explore. E006's +0.66 pp confounded Muon, batch 1024→2000 and an RNG re-draw. On the current tip (the H2.6.2 successor if kept, else E027), replace Muon on the conv filters with Nesterov SGD (momentum 0.9, as in the E005 recipe). Scale the conv-filter lr and wd the way E005's code did for batch 1024, linearly scaled to batch 2000. The frozen group-1 param group keeps its annealed schedule. Batch, epochs, resolution phases, freeze, Lookahead, LS and the SGD groups stay unchanged. Recapture every graph in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time falls about 2–4% (the NS overhead, about 0.15–0.2 s). Held-out mean falls 0.2–0.6 pp (median about −0.35), which would support H1.2.2 and confirm Muon as an accuracy source worth more than its time. A loss of 0.15 pp or less means E006's gain came from batch size or the re-draw, so dropping Muon is a free 3% cut. That would also reopen batch tuning under SGD (H5).

drop.reason: The committee gives it 0/4 improve votes and expects about −0.2 pp. The base's population mean (held-out 0.7526) is already below the 0.7545 keep gate, so the run cannot be kept, and its rate (about 1.2 s/pp) cannot be told apart from the epoch dial. The freeze-dose idea (H2.6.4) on the freeze successor is a better-rate time lever. Re-propose the 20 px extension only once a base with held-out ≥0.7555 exists.

The committee gives it 0/4 improve votes, a median of about +0.05 pp (flat) and +0.5–1% time. It cannot produce a time win, and a gain of ≥0.2 pp is outside every member's range. Low expected improvement and low information.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is E027: 5.88 s, held-out mean 0.7526, so it is feasible only on lucky seeds. E028's group-1 freeze saves 0.52 s at no cost in population accuracy, the best exchange rate found so far. The plan is to stack that free lever with the cheapest accuracy booster, epochs. The top priority is H2.6.2: freeze plus 9.25 true epochs, predicted at about 5.7 s with held-out about 0.7545.

Next come two near-free cuts:
- **H3.2.1:** a prepare change on the systems side only, with bit-identical math. It saves about 0.03–0.1 s and also tests W5's crux, whether a change that keeps the math identical keeps the tip's per-seed outcomes.
- **H2.6.3:** stop the whitening-bias gradient early.

Further cuts to the stem's backward pass:
- **H2.6.4:** start the freeze earlier, at 60% of steps.
- **H2.6.5:** during the frozen phase, put group-1 BN in eval mode and fold it into the conv.

H4.3.2 then validates any kept candidate on fresh seeds 13–22, since seeds 3–12 now carry a winner's curse.

Two explore ideas round out the queue:
- **H6.3.1:** profile kernel classes per layer group. This sets the value of the stem levers and the risk that the SXM4-to-PCIe transfer shifts the time ranking.
- **H1.2.2:** replace Muon with SGD. This tests whether E006's Muon gain was real or confounded; if it was confounded, dropping Muon saves about 3% for free.

I dropped I050 and I051:
- **I050 (longer 20 px phase):** the committee gave it 0 improve votes. Its expected loss of about 0.2 pp can't be absorbed at a held-out mean of 0.7526, and the freeze-dose idea is a better time lever.
- **I051 (per-resolution whitening):** 0 improve votes, it adds time, and the expected effect is flat.

I049 (late label-smoothing removal) is still running.
